page: Microsoft Azure D16d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical x86_64 cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache, backed by vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Memory performance testing demonstrates an uncached read bandwidth of 80.99 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 43.83 GB/sec, placing the memory subsystem within the average middle tier. For ephemeral data operations, the instance features a dedicated local 644 GB SSD, eliminating external disk network roundtrips for temporary files and swap spaces.

Benchmark outcomes show uniform middle-tier throughput across common processing workloads. The instance registered a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,845 and a PassMark CPU score of 15,473.34. In transactional scenarios, it achieved 13.99 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 11.82 GB/sec static web serving throughput. Natural language inference benchmarks reveal a tradeoff: prompt processing for a medium 7B model scored in the bottom 25 percent at 24.49 tokens per second, while generation remained at 10.08 tokens per second.

Given its balanced compute-to-memory allocation and included fast local disk, the D16d_v4 offers reliable hardware density and cost efficiency for applications that need local scratch storage without requiring specialized accelerators. Typical deployment targets include relational database instances, intermediate caching servers, continuous integration build runners, and general web application tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure D16d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine engineered for balanced computing environments, featuring an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz. It is provisioned with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 64.0 GB of system memory, and a direct-attached 644 GB SSD for fast local scratch storage. The architecture includes AVX-512 vector acceleration and delivered 14,893.66 on stress-ng multi-core and 7,845 on Geekbench multi-core evaluations. With 80.99 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth and throughput of 13.99 million Redis operations per second, its performance across transactional and computational tests resides consistently in the middle tier. However, heavier AI workloads such as 7B parameter LLM prompt processing exhibit weaker performance due to the lack of hardware accelerators. D16d_v4 is best suited for enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, relational database servers, and caching workloads requiring integrated local disk capacity.
